blocks.text: 1. Relation Extraction
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863055-46286121.png

Entity Extraction closed by explaining that relation extraction needs already identified entities to connect together. Relation Extraction, identifying how already extracted entities connect to each other, is that second step, completing the triples a graph is built from.
It reads the text around two mentioned entities to determine what relationship, if any, actually links them.
2. Relations Connect Two Already Known Entities
As covered generally in Knowledge Graphs as edges representing relationships, relation extraction never invents new entities of its own.
It only looks for connections between entities that entity extraction already identified.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","What it produces"],"rows":[["Entity extraction","Individual entities as candidate nodes"],["Relation extraction","Named connections between those existing entities"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Naming The Relationship Type
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863057-807808151.png
As with facts as connected triples in Knowledge Graphs, a found relationship must be labeled with a specific, verb-like name, such as supplies or acquired.
A vague or generic label makes the resulting triple far less useful to query.
4. Direction Matters In A Relationship
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863058-687248280.png
As with edges representing relationships in Knowledge Graphs, most relationships are directional, not symmetric.
Falcon Cloud supplies Acme Corp is not the same statement as Acme Corp supplies Falcon Cloud.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: The relationship supplies points from supplier to customer, so extracting it in the wrong direction produces a factually backwards triple even though both entities were correctly identified.

blocks.text: 5. Proximity Alone Is Not A Relationship

blocks.alt: Proximity Alone Is Not A Relationship
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863058-292133829.png
Two entities appearing in the same sentence does not automatically mean they are meaningfully related.
The actual wording between them has to support a specific, real relationship.
6. Relation Extraction Methods Vary In Cost

blocks.alt: Relation Extraction Methods Vary In Cost
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863059-73454019.png
As with extraction methods varying in cost in Entity Extraction, a pattern based extractor is fast but misses relationships phrased in unexpected ways.
A trained extraction model catches more phrasing variety at higher cost.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Method","Tradeoff"],"rows":[["Pattern based extractor","Fast, but misses unexpected phrasing"],["Trained extraction model","Catches more phrasing variety, costs more"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Incorrect Relations Corrupt Traversal
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863059-274939909.png
As with an error in an early hop propagating forward in Multi-Hop RAG, a wrongly extracted relationship creates an edge that leads a later traversal query astray.
The graph becomes actively misleading rather than just incomplete.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A backwards or mislabeled relationship edge is worse than a missing edge, since a later graph traversal follows it as if it were true, actively misleading rather than simply leaving a gap.

blocks.text: 8. Relation Extraction Completes The Triple
As with facts as connected triples in Knowledge Graphs, two already extracted entities plus one confirmed relationship form one complete, insertable triple.
Entity extraction and relation extraction together produce exactly what graph construction needs.
9. Recognizing When Careful Relation Extraction Is Worth The Added Effort

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Careful Relation Extraction Is Worth The Added Effort
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863060-380840207.png
A graph meant to support multi-hop traversal queries needs accurate relations.
A graph used only for simple entity lookups, by contrast, tolerates looser relation extraction.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Treating any two entities in the same sentence as automatically related.
Extracting a relationship without confirming which direction it actually points.
Using a vague relationship label that loses meaning when queried later.
Inserting an unverified extracted relationship directly into the graph without any check.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Relation extraction identifies how already extracted entities connect to each other.
It never invents new entities, only finding connections between entities already extracted.
A found relationship must be labeled with a specific, verb-like name, not a vague term.
Most relationships are directional; the subject and object are not interchangeable.
Two entities appearing near each other does not automatically mean they are related.
Pattern based extractors are fast but miss unexpected phrasing; trained models cost more but generalize.
A wrongly extracted relationship misleads later graph traversal rather than just leaving a gap.
An extracted entity pair plus a confirmed relationship forms exactly one complete, insertable triple.
